---
title: "check-static-figures.yml"
---

Diff-scoped check that flags an interactive figure
with no noninteractive version in static formats.
The lab's rule (Ezra, 2026-11-10) is that static formats,
such as PDF, Word, and PowerPoint,
still render 3D plots and other interactive figures, as noninteractive versions.
This implements
[gha#1822](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1822);
the writing rule is in
[psw#568](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/psw/pull/568).
It warns by default while the notes repositories catch up.

It reports two findings:

- **A placeholder note.**
  A line that says "see the HTML version"
  (or the web, website, online, or "HTML or slides" version),
  in prose or in a code chunk that prints it.
  It is reported per line, even when the file has a static version elsewhere,
  because the note is still what a reader of that tab sees.
- **An HTML-only interactive figure.**
  A code fence that builds a plotly, htmlwidgets, leaflet, or rgl figure
  and runs only in HTML output,
  in a file that draws no static version.

A fence runs only in HTML output
when its `#| eval:` option calls `is_html_output()` without negating it,
or when it sits in a `.content-visible when-format="html"` (or `"revealjs"`) div
or a `.content-hidden unless-format="html"` div.
A file has a static version when another fence runs only outside HTML output
(a negated `is_html_output()`, `is_latex_output()`,
or a div shown only in a static format)
and draws a plot, such as `persp(`, `ggplot(`, `plt.`, `plot(`,
`plotly::save_image(`, or `webshot`.
A chunk that only prints a note is not a plot.

A widget that runs in every format is not flagged,
because knitr screenshots it in static output when webshot2 is installed.
Neither is a chunk that branches on `knitr::is_html_output()` inside its code,
returning the widget in HTML and a ggplot otherwise.

A file holding an HTML comment `<!-- static-version: reason -->`
with a non-empty reason is exempt from both findings,
for a figure that has no meaningful still image.
Use `paths-ignore` to exempt whole paths.

## Limits

The check matches call names in the source, not what a render draws,
so it has two known limits.

- A widget call inside a code comment, such as `# plotly::plot_ly(z = z)`,
  still counts as an interactive figure.
  Delete the commented-out call, or add the `static-version` exemption.
- A static version is judged per file, not per figure.
  Any plot call in a fence that runs only outside HTML output,
  including a bare `ax.` method or `include_graphics(`,
  counts as the static version of every HTML-only figure in the file.
  So a file with two HTML-only figures and one static plot is not flagged.

## Scope

Only a finding whose fence or line holds a line a pull request adds is reported,
so untouched figures are not reflagged.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new, and a blank added line is not content.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed,
the check skips instead of scanning the whole tree.
It logs the skip, as a warning annotation when a given `base-ref` cannot be diffed.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file on purpose,
which measures how many existing figures lack a static version.
Every run that does not skip prints how many lines, files,
and interactive figures it examined.

## Inputs

| Input          | Type    | Default       | Description |
| -------------- | ------- | ------------- | ----------- |
| `globs`        | string  | `'*.qmd'`     | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore` | string  | `''`          | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`         | boolean | `false`       | Fail the workflow on a finding. The default is warning annotations only. |
| `whole-tree`   | boolean | `false`       | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string | `'3.x'`      | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | empty (`CI_RUNNER` variable, else `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-static-figures.yml in your repo.
name: Check static figures

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-static-figures.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   fail: true         # block on a finding (defaults to false)
```
